meta.siteTagline: Practical AI, controlled delivery and usable products

home.headline: I help teams turn AI usage and prototypes into something genuinely usable.
home.subheadline: As a senior developer, I step in to structure, harden or build AI workflows and products without black boxes, unnecessary debt or hype.

proof.title: Operational proof before polished public case studies
proof.intro: I prefer to show method, systems and guardrails: how AI is scoped, verified and connected to a real business workflow.

publicProject.title: Public project in progress: Rusty Art
publicProject.description: Rusty Art is an ongoing public project. I use it as a live ground for testing workflows, orchestration and product iteration patterns around AI.

publicWork.label: Public work signal
publicWork.value: Rusty Art is live and inspectable
publicWork.description: A public project shows an AI workflow in progress instead of relying only on sales copy.

tools.label: Tools in use
tools.description: The site and proof surface use real delivery, automation, versioned-content and quality-control tools.

process.label: Process artifacts
process.description: Important decisions are framed by sources of truth, human review and checkpoints before action.

openclaw.title: OpenClaw setup used daily
openclaw.description: A working environment with specialist assistants, scheduled reports, durable memory and gated actions: a concrete proof of operational AI capability.

method.title: Human-led AI delivery
method.description: Explicit sources of truth, versioned prompts, quality review, guardrails and human escalation when the workflow gets sensitive.

execution.title: Full execution capacity
execution.description: When a use case is validated, I can carry it through code, automation, web integration and deployment.

web.title: Start from a real use case instead of a trend
web.body: The right starting point is not the AI tool of the month, but the problem worth solving and the value expected for the team or the user.

realtime.title: Keep technical decisions readable even when delivery accelerates
realtime.body: AI can help move faster. It should not make code, trade-offs or maintenance harder to own afterwards.

trust.title: Build something that can be resumed and improved later
trust.body: The result should stay understandable, maintainable and clean enough to evolve without pain later on.

trust.eyebrow: When AI moves faster than structure
trust.title: The situations where structure needs to be restored
trust.intro: Many teams experiment, patch things together and move faster with AI. The real challenge comes after that: making it understandable, reliable and usable inside a product or business context.

direct.label: Ideas, prototypes or automations move quickly, but without a base that is really clear enough to last

delivery.label: AI speeds parts of the work up, but code, decisions and ownership become harder to follow

quality.value: A need to make it real
quality.label: A first version exists, but it now needs to become cleaner, more maintainable and more credible in production

process.title: Three ways I usually step into an AI topic
process.intro: I usually step in either to bring order to an existing AI usage, to harden a base that already exists, or to build an AI feature that serves a real use case.
process.primaryCta: Discuss your AI project or prototype

discovery.title: Structure AI usage that is getting hard to manage
discovery.body: Clarify where AI genuinely helps in delivery, production or operations, and stop it from becoming an extra layer of confusion.

points.goals: Identify the steps where AI creates real leverage instead of extra noise.
points.queries: Make usages, roles and limits easier for the team to understand.
points.plan: Put a frame around it that remains usable as the project grows or changes hands.

build.title: Take over a prototype or implementation that already exists
build.body: When a first version is already there, the work is often about restoring readability, structure and a level of quality that can support a real product path.

stackItems.realtime: Make the project easier to maintain

launch.title: Build an AI feature or tool that serves a real use case
launch.body: When something needs to be built, the goal is not to add AI for the sake of it. It is to design something useful, understandable and usable over time.

verify.body: Define what AI should actually improve for the user or the team.

publish.body: Keep the architecture, decisions and ownership readable even when delivery speeds up.

measure.body: Make sure the project can be resumed, iterated on or hardened later without starting over a few weeks later.
